events.title: Goldey, Associate Warden, et al. v. Fields, Andrew III, et al.
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted certiorari in the case of Goldey, Associate Warden, et al. v. Fields, Andrew III, et al., reversed the judgment of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit, and remanded the case. The Court determined that an Eighth Amendment excessive-force Bivens claim should not be extended, emphasizing the role of Congress in creating causes of action.
events.why_relevant: This decision reinforces the limitations on judicially created causes of action under Bivens.

events.title: Invitation for Amicus Curiae in NRSC v. FEC

FEC, et al., docket number 24-621, inviting Roman Martinez, Esquire, of Washington, D.C., to brief and argue the case as amicus curiae in support of the judgment below. This procedural action allows for additional legal perspectives to be considered by the Court in its deliberations.
events.why_relevant: The invitation for amicus curiae participation can influence the Court's understanding and decision-making in the case.

events.title: Certiorari Granted in Consolidated Cases Involving NJ Transit Corp.

Colt, Jeffrey, et al., limited to the question of whether the New Jersey Transit Corporation is an arm of the State of New Jersey for interstate sovereign immunity purposes. The cases are consolidated for one hour of oral argument.
events.why_relevant: The decision will clarify the legal status of NJ Transit Corp. regarding sovereign immunity, impacting state liability and governance.

events.title: Certiorari Granted in M & K Employee Solutions v. Trustees of the IAM Pension
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted certiorari in the case of M & K Employee Solutions, et al. v. Trustees of the IAM Pension, limited to the question of whether 29 U.S.C. §1391 requires the computation of withdrawal liability based on actuarial assumptions adopted before the end of the plan year or allows for assumptions adopted after the year-end based on available information. This decision will clarify the interpretation of federal pension law regarding actuarial assumptions.
events.why_relevant: The decision will impact how pension withdrawal liabilities are calculated, affecting employers and pension plans.
